about: In communion with the whole Church, the prayer honors the memory of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Saint Joseph, the Apostles, and the martyrs. After naming the saints, it asks God to surround the faithful with His protection through their merits and prayers.

seg.tr: Joined in communion, and venerating the memory, first of all, of the glorious ever Virgin Mary, Mother of God and our Lord Jesus Christ;

ex.w001: The participle continues the prayer of the Canon: its unexpressed subject is the we who offer the sacrifice (offérimus), not a separate group called communicants.
ex.w004: Joined to Communicántes by et and governing memóriam: the same unexpressed we venerate the memory of Mary and the saints.

seg.tr: and also blessed Joseph, Spouse of that same Virgin,
and of Your blessed Apostles and Martyrs: Peter and Paul, Andrew, James, John, Thomas, James, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Simon, and Thaddeus;

a.g: of Your blessed apostles and martyrs

ex.w033: The list names twelve Apostles, including Paul rather than Matthias.
ex.w035: The first of the two Jameses in this list: James the Greater, John’s brother, the son of Zebedee.
ex.w038: His place in the list distinguishes him from “Iacóbi” (w035).

seg.tr: Linus, Cletus, Clement, Sixtus, Cornelius, Cyprian, Lawrence, Chrysogonus, John and Paul, Cosmas and Damian;

ex.w045: Linus begins the second group of twelve names in this prayer.
ex.w055: John and Paul here are Roman martyrs commemorated together on 26 June, not the Apostles named earlier.

seg.tr: and all Your saints; grant, by their merits and prayers, that we may be fortified in all things with the aid of Your protection.

a.g: we may be defended by the help of Your protection

seg.tr: Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.
